title: AI underwriting for lenders and insurers: what to automate first
description: Where AI pays in underwriting: the reading, not the decision. 19 tools checked, the US and EU rules, our benchmark data and three builds.
summary: AI underwriting does the reading: it pulls the facts from applications, statements and broker emails so your underwriters decide faster[^13][^22]. It fits small-business lenders, life insurers with a rules engine[^20], and commercial insurers and MGAs whose underwriters spend hours keying broker submissions[^7]. P&C underwriters spend about 4 in 10 hours on admin, and the decision stays explainable with a person accountable[^1][^7][^4][^2].
verdict: The money is hours back for deciding. P&C underwriters spend about 39% of their time on admin and other non-core work, the paperwork AI can take on[^1][^8][^7].
Start with the reading: statements and tax returns for lenders, broker submissions for commercial insurers and MGAs (managing general agents)[^22], referred-case evidence for life insurers[^19].
AI reads long financial PDFs well: the two best models made zero mistakes on 30 fund reports, answers locked in advance[^13]. Those weren't loan files, so benchmark on your own[^13].
Keep the decision with an explainable model and a named underwriter. US lenders owe decline reasons; New York expects the same from insurers[^4][^17][^2].
First step: benchmark AI on 50 past files from one line or one branch before you buy. Vendors' faster-quote figures are their own customers' claims[^21][^28].

pickElse: Consumer lending where the score is the product: start with the AI credit scoring guide[^30]. The decline reasons are the regulated part[^4][^17].

Life and health insurer: start from a rules engine such as Swiss Re MagnumXP or Munich Re ALLFINANZ[^18][^20]. AI earns its keep summarising the evidence on referred cases so the underwriter decides faster, not making the call[^19][^20].

Commercial insurer or MGA swamped by broker submissions: an off-the-shelf intake product (Cytora, Convr, FurtherAI, Sixfold) may beat a build[^23][^24][^22][^21]. Benchmark one on 50 of your own past submissions before you sign.
The question is price, not whether to take the risk: look at actuarial pricing platforms such as Akur8, Earnix or hyperexponential[^25][^26][^27].

ownData.title: Which underwriting steps AI can take on today
ownData.intro: Our read of each step, built from our own benchmark of AI reading long financial documents[^13] and the published studies below. That benchmark used public private-fund reports, not loan or insurance files[^13].
rows: Intake: read applications, broker emails, forms
Yes, with a second model checking
Two models, 0 mistakes on 30 reports with answers locked in advance (FinExtractBench)[^13]
Pull facts from statements, returns and loss runs (claims history)
Yes, if every fact cites its page and quote
The top nine tools were within 2 facts of each other (FinExtractBench hard round)[^13]
Pick the right number among look-alike tables
Not alone; flag these for a person
7 of 10 tools took the wrong table on one 57-page report (FinExtractBench)[^13]
Chat models rated their wrong answers 70 to 100 (FinExtractBench)[^13]
Yes, if its stated reasons are the factors it scored[^17]; logistic regression stays the most transparent choice[^15]

A standard machine-learning model beat chat models at predicting loan defaults, and the same method tops a credit-scoring review[^14][^15]. MassMutual's machine-learned life score beat traditional underwriting on claims[^5][^33].
A person, using the model's reasons
Reg B (the US rule on credit decisions) requires specific reasons[^4][^17]. New York's insurance regulator (NYDFS) expects them in Circular Letter 7[^2].
ownData.note: Your documents will differ, which is why the first step of any build is a benchmark on your own files.

example.input: A small-business loan application, 12 months of bank statements and two years of tax returns.
example.output: Average monthly revenue, existing debt payments and two flagged risks, each with its page and quote. Plus a draft risk score with its main reasons, for the underwriter to accept or change.

recipes.name: 1. Commercial insurance: submission intake
recipes.when: Commercial insurers and MGAs whose underwriters spend hours keying broker submissions; admin takes 41% to 43% of their time[^7].
flow: Broker email, forms and loss runs (claims history) land in a queue the ops lead owns
AI extracts each fact with page and quote
AI checks appetite (the risks you want to write) and clearance (has another broker already sent this risk?); an underwriting assistant resolves flagged facts
Underwriter works the queue best fit first and decides
recipes.cost: Reading cost $0.12 to $0.15 per fund report with the two best models in our benchmark, not per loan file[^13]. Intake products publish no price[^24]; a Zavient build is quoted per job, not listed here.

recipes.name: 2. Small-business lending: file to decision
recipes.when: Lenders whose underwriters spend the day reading statements and returns.
flow: Bank statements and tax returns land in a queue the ops lead owns
AI spreads statements and returns into your template, meaning it copies each figure into your standard credit-analysis layout
An underwriting assistant clears flagged facts
Explainable model drafts a score with its reasons
recipes.cost: Under $0.01 to about $0.30 per fund report to read with current models in our benchmark, not per loan file[^13]. The build, including a scorecard you own, is quoted per job, not listed here.

recipes.name: 3. Life insurance: evidence summary for the rules engine
recipes.when: Life and health carriers with an existing rules engine.
flow: Application and medical evidence land in a queue the ops lead owns
Clean cases: offer drafted, an underwriter spot-checks a sample
Others: referred to an underwriter, who decides
recipes.cost: Rules engines such as MagnumXP and ALLFINANZ publish no price; you contact the vendor[^18][^20]. The AI reading layer is quoted per job, and you can benchmark and swap it.

rules.name: Regulation B, 12 CFR 1002.9
rules.what: US lenders must give notice of a decline within 30 days, with the specific main reasons or the right to get them[^4]. For a scoring model, the reasons must be the factors it actually scored[^17].

rules.name: NYDFS Circular Letter No. 7
rules.what: New York insurers should test AI and outside data for unfair discrimination and keep board oversight[^2]. They stay responsible for vendor tools and should give specific reasons and data sources for adverse decisions[^2].

rules.name: NAIC Model Bulletin on AI
rules.what: The NAIC (the US state insurance regulators' body) asks insurers to keep a written AI program with governance, risk controls, testing and vendor oversight[^34]. 30 US jurisdictions have adopted it[^9][^10]. California, Colorado and New York have their own rules instead[^9].

rules.name: Colorado SB21-169
rules.status: Life; auto and health from 15 Oct 2025
rules.what: Insurers must test outside data and models for unfair discrimination, fix harm found and show the Division how they test[^3][^16].

rules.name: EU AI Act, Annex III
rules.what: Credit scoring of people and life and health insurance risk pricing are high-risk uses[^6]. Those rules apply from 2 December 2027[^11][^12]. High-risk systems need automatic logs and human oversight, so plan both now if you operate in the EU[^35][^36].

howToTest: Before any AI, time 50 files from one line or one branch as your team handles them today. Record hours per file, decision turnaround and how many in-appetite files are left without a quote or decision.
Then take 50 past files with known outcomes, including your messiest scans and longest packets.
Have your underwriters write the right value for every fact before any AI reads the files, and lock that answer key.
Run each tool on the same files. Count wrong facts apart from blanks, and require a page and quote for every fact.
For scoring, compare an explainable model with your current method on the same past files. Check that the decline reasons make sense to an underwriter.
Measure cost and time per file, and how many files still need a person. Report files decided per underwriter per week, decision turnaround and in-appetite submissions left unquoted, before and after.

buyVsBuild.buy: Buy when your line is standard, the vendor already handles your submission formats, and you are happy to run inside its workbench.
buyVsBuild.build: Build when your own loss history and appetite are your edge, or when you need the reading step to feed systems you already own. The reading layer is swappable: in our benchmark the top nine models were within 2 facts of each other[^13]. The decision logic is yours.

watchOuts: You stay responsible for a vendor's model. New York and the NAIC bulletin both expect audit rights in vendor contracts where available[^2][^34].
Models can carry past bias into new decisions. New York and Colorado expect insurers to test for unfair outcomes across groups before use and on a schedule after[^2][^16].
A model's confidence score is not a warning sign. In our benchmark, wrong answers came back rated 70 to 100[^13].
Vendor claims such as faster quotes are the vendor's own figures[^24], often from chosen customers[^21][^28]. Ask for a benchmark on your own files.
Flagged facts need an owner: in our benchmark, look-alike tables tripped 7 of 10 tools on one report[^13]. Count flags per file, multiply by weekly files and name who clears them.
